description: How organisations use digital technology to change their strategy, products and ways of working, and how new ventures are built and measured. Students diagnose cases, model business processes and platforms in the diagram studio, and make decisions in branching scenarios scored against a rubric.
modelledOn: Osterwalder and Pigneur, Business Model Generation
Cagan, Inspired: How to Create Tech Products Customers Love
outcomes: Assess an organisation's digital maturity and propose a business model change using a canvas and recognised model patterns.
Plan and govern a change programme, with stakeholder analysis, adoption drivers and a communication plan.
Apply design thinking, lean experiments and agile delivery to take an idea from problem to tested prototype.
Analyse a platform business, including network effects, governance and ecosystem partners.
Build a financial and non-financial case for a digital initiative and track its value with metrics.
Present a prioritised transformation roadmap to an executive audience and defend its assumptions.

units.title: Digital strategy and business models
topics: Digital technologies as drivers of transformation: mobile money, cloud, data and AI
Digital maturity models and readiness assessment
Business Model Canvas and value proposition design
Digital business model patterns: freemium, subscription, marketplace and pay-as-you-go
Aligning IT and business strategy: strategy maps and capability maps
Case studies: digital change in African banking, agriculture and logistics

units.title: Change management and adoption
topics: Eight-step change model and the unfreeze-change-refreeze view of change
Stakeholder analysis: power-interest grid and communication plans
Technology acceptance: TAM, UTAUT and the diffusion of innovations curve
Resistance to change, digital skills gaps and training programmes
Transformation governance: steering committees, transformation office and RACI charts

units.title: Innovation processes and design thinking
topics: Types of innovation: incremental, radical, disruptive and open innovation
Design thinking stages: empathise, define, ideate, prototype, test
User research: interviews, personas and journey maps
Lean startup: minimum viable product, build-measure-learn and pivots
Idea portfolios: impact-effort matrix and stage-gate funnels
Agile delivery and DevOps as enablers of continuous innovation

units.title: Platform and ecosystem strategies
topics: Platform versus pipeline businesses; two-sided markets and network effects
Platform governance, open APIs and open banking
Ecosystem orchestration: partners, complementors, mobile network operators and fintechs
The chicken-and-egg problem: bootstrapping and pricing each side
Platform risks: lock-in, multi-homing, regulation and data protection

units.title: Digital product management
topics: Product lifecycle and the product manager role
Product vision, roadmaps and OKRs
Backlog prioritisation: MoSCoW, RICE scoring and satisfaction-based feature classification
Product analytics: funnels, retention cohorts and A/B tests
Pricing and monetisation of digital products
Scaling, technical debt, product-market fit signals and sunsetting

units.title: Technology entrepreneurship and startups
topics: Opportunity recognition and problem-solution fit
Founding teams, equity splits and legal forms of business in Ghana
Financing: bootstrapping, grants, angel and venture capital, crowdfunding
Unit economics: customer acquisition cost, lifetime value, burn rate and runway
Pitching: the pitch deck and investor questions
Startup ecosystems in Africa: hubs, incubators and accelerators

units.title: Measuring the value of digital initiatives
topics: Business case: cost-benefit analysis, NPV, IRR and payback period
Balanced scorecard and KPIs for digital initiatives
Benefits realisation management and value tracking
Risk, scenario analysis and real options
Digital ethics, inclusion and sustainability impact

units.title: Capstone: building a transformation roadmap
topics: Diagnosing an organisation: maturity scores and pain points
Building a prioritised roadmap and initiative portfolio
Presenting the case to an executive board
Review and reflection on the course cases

schedule.title: Digital drivers, maturity and strategy alignment
schedule.exercise: Pick a Ghanaian organisation, list the digital technologies that threaten or help it, score its maturity on a five-dimension model and draw a strategy map linking IT capabilities to business goals.

tasks.title: Read a short case on a mobile money rollout and choose, for five decisions, the technology driver that best explains the change, scoring against the rubric
Assess a regional bank's digital maturity from interview evidence across five dimensions, justify each score and pick the two weakest areas to fix first
Draw a capability map and strategy map for a cooperative, then show which IT capabilities are missing for three stated strategic goals

schedule.title: Business models and patterns
schedule.exercise: Fill in a Business Model Canvas for an agritech startup, then redesign its revenue model using two other patterns and compare the effect on customers and costs.

tasks.title: Complete the nine blocks of a Business Model Canvas for a mobile airtime reseller and check that each customer segment has a value proposition
Choose between freemium, subscription and pay-as-you-go pricing for a farm advisory app in a branching case and justify each choice with the evidence given
Evaluate a bank's plan to launch agent banking, weigh three competing business model options and defend the recommendation against a board challenge

schedule.title: Leading change
schedule.exercise: Map a failed system rollout onto the eight change steps to find which were skipped, and build a power-interest grid and communication plan for a hospital moving to electronic records.

tasks.title: Read a case of a stalled ERP rollout and order the eight change steps, marking which step the project skipped and why it mattered
Build a power-interest grid for twelve stakeholders of a district hospital system and write a one-line engagement approach for each quadrant
Use adoption survey evidence to explain why nurses reject a new app, apply TAM and UTAUT constructs, and choose interventions within a fixed training budget

schedule.title: Adoption, skills and governance
schedule.exercise: Draft a training and support plan for a digital skills gap in a district assembly, and write a RACI chart and steering committee terms of reference for the transformation.

tasks.title: Draw a RACI chart for six activities of a payroll system migration with exactly one accountable person per activity
Respond to staff resistance in a branching case, choosing training, incentives and communication steps, and compare final adoption scores across two attempts
Design the governance structure for a bank-wide transformation, resolve a conflict between two directors, and justify decision rights in the rubric

schedule.title: Innovation types and design thinking
schedule.exercise: Classify six real products by innovation type, then interview two potential users about an everyday transport problem and turn the findings into a persona and a journey map.

tasks.title: Classify eight product launches as incremental, radical or disruptive, and explain each answer using the evidence in the case notes
Turn six interview notes about trotro commuting into a persona and a journey map, marking the three largest pain points
Run a design thinking project in a branching case, deciding at each stage what to research and prototype, and defend how you reframed the problem

schedule.title: Lean experiments, prioritisation and agile delivery
schedule.exercise: Write the riskiest assumption for a market-price app, design a minimum viable product test with a pass mark, and rank ten ideas with an impact-effort matrix.

tasks.title: Place ten product ideas on an impact-effort matrix and mark the quick wins, big bets and ideas to drop
Choose experiments for three assumptions of a startup, read the results and decide for each whether to persevere, pivot or stop
Draw a delivery pipeline from idea to release with sprint cadence and automated testing, and mark where each step shortens feedback time

schedule.title: Platforms and ecosystems
schedule.exercise: Draw the ecosystem of a mobile money platform with its participants and money and data flows, then propose a plan to attract merchants first and users second, and list three platform risks.

tasks.title: Draw a two-sided market diagram for a ride-hailing platform, label the cross-side network effects and give one example of a same-side effect
Map the ecosystem of a mobile money service with banks, agents and developers, and trace how a merchant payment flows through it
Bootstrap a marketplace in a branching case by choosing which side to subsidise, setting prices and comparing growth after ten simulated months

schedule.title: Product management foundations
schedule.exercise: Write a product vision and quarterly OKRs for a school fees payment app, and prioritise a backlog of twelve features using RICE scores.

tasks.title: Draw the lifecycle of a digital product from idea to retirement and mark which decisions a product manager owns at each stage
Set a product vision and three OKRs with measurable key results in a branching case, and revise them after a mid-quarter shock
Score twelve backlog features with RICE, test how the ranking changes when reach estimates move by twenty percent, and report which choices are stable

schedule.title: Analytics, pricing and scaling
schedule.exercise: Read a funnel and retention table for a savings app, pick one improvement experiment, set its sample size and success criterion, and choose a price for a premium tier.

tasks.title: Compute the conversion rate at each step of a sign-up funnel from given counts and find the step with the largest drop-off
Set prices for three tiers of a digital service in a branching case, observe demand responses and defend the revenue-maximising choice
Analyse an A/B test with a two-proportion test and confidence interval, decide whether to ship, and state what extra data would change your mind

schedule.title: Opportunities, founders and ecosystems
schedule.exercise: Interview a small trader about a daily problem, write a problem statement with evidence, and draft a founder agreement covering roles, equity and vesting under a registered company form.

tasks.title: Compare five opportunity ideas against evidence of customer pain and willingness to pay, and pick the one with the best problem-solution fit
Negotiate an equity split among three cofounders with unequal contributions in a branching case, and test its fairness over a later funding round
Map the startup ecosystem of a Ghanaian city with hubs, funders, universities and regulators, and mark the gap that most limits startup growth

schedule.title: Financing, unit economics and pitching
schedule.exercise: Compute customer acquisition cost, lifetime value and runway for a delivery startup, choose a financing route, and prepare a five-minute pitch with a ten-slide outline.

tasks.title: Compute CAC, LTV and the LTV to CAC ratio for a startup from a monthly table and state whether the model is viable
Choose between grants, angel money and a bank loan for a seed-stage startup in a branching case and compare dilution and risk
Pitch to a simulated investor panel, answer six hard questions on market size, margins and competition, and improve the pitch after feedback

schedule.title: Measuring and proving value
schedule.exercise: Build a five-year business case with NPV and payback for a digital land registry project, define a balanced scorecard, and list three ethical risks and mitigations.

tasks.title: Compute NPV, payback period and IRR for a five-year cash flow table of a digital project at a ten percent discount rate
Build a balanced scorecard with four perspectives and two KPIs each for a mobile health programme, linking each KPI to a strategic objective
Run a scenario analysis on a digital initiative with Monte Carlo cost and benefit ranges, and report the chance that NPV is negative

schedule.title: Capstone: transformation roadmap
schedule.exercise: Diagnose a case organisation, build a three-year roadmap with prioritised initiatives, value estimates and risks, and present it in ten minutes to a mock board.

tasks.title: Score a case company on maturity dimensions from evidence in documents and interviews, and list its five most important pain points
Draw a three-year roadmap with eight initiatives, dependencies and milestones, and mark the critical path using the diagram tools
Present the roadmap to a simulated executive board, handle objections on cost, risk and staffing, and refine the plan against the scoring rubric
